findings.title: BrickLink to remain offline until Monday with no further explanation from LEGO
findings.summary_md: Brick Fanatics reported on 6 November 2026 that BrickLink would remain offline until Monday, with no further explanation from the LEGO Group beyond an earlier notice that the marketplace would be down for most of the day for necessary work. The planned return window had already been extended once, and the site stayed unavailable past the end of that window. The report describes the outage as still unexplained at that point, with the platform showing only a maintenance notice.

findings.title: BrickLink downtime continues
findings.summary_md: Brickset reported on 9 November 2026 that BrickLink had been down since late the previous week and would remain offline until at least Wednesday evening. The post stated that no announcement or communication about the cause had been made, and it noted that Brickset hotlinks minifigure images from BrickLink servers and uses the BrickLink API for prices and availability, so its own listings were missing images and price data. Brickset pointed readers to BrickOwl, the independent marketplace, as the working alternative.

findings.title: Is BrickLink Down? What Happened in the November 2026 Outage
findings.summary_md: BrickReport published an outage explainer on 10 November 2026 describing BrickLink going offline late on Thursday 5 November, with every page on the site redirecting to a temporarily unavailable notice. At that point LEGO had given no reason beyond detecting unusual activity, and the post tracked the repeatedly moved return estimates. The article was updated after service was restored and after LEGO confirmed what data had been accessed.

findings.title: BrickLink outage hits day 5 as a LEGO seller reports 52% drop
findings.summary_md: On 10 November 2026 this report covered the fifth day of the BrickLink outage and quoted seller Simon Webster of DSLS Bricks, whose overall sales revenue was down 52% against the same four days of the previous November while his BrickOwl sales were up 79%. It cited Brick-Tracker's count of about 18,750 shops in BrickLink's last public store directory, including roughly 1,800 in Germany, and noted LEGO bought BrickLink in November 2019 with more than 10,000 sellers across over 70 countries. The piece also recalled the outage of 3 to 8 November 2023, which followed a threat and ransom demand and was later attributed to credential stuffing, with every user forced to reset a password.

findings.title: Bricklink is still down due to a suspected hacking/cybersecurity issue
findings.summary_md: Jay's Brick Blog reported on 11 November 2026 that BrickLink had been down for almost a week, having gone offline on 5 November, and that the latest promised return date of 11 November had passed with no new date given. The post noted that BrickLink had by then said it detected unusual activity on the platform, after an earlier period with no communication at all. It compared the timing to the early November 2023 outage and criticised the lack of notice to sellers during one of the busiest shopping periods of the year.

findings.title: Lego marketplace BrickLink offline after 'unusual activity' detected
findings.summary_md: The BBC reported on 11 November 2026 that LEGO had taken BrickLink offline after detecting what it called unusual activity on the platform, without confirming whether the site had been breached or whether customer data was affected. LEGO's homepage statement said it wanted to fully understand what happened by containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues. The article noted the site had been down for three days and that a collector, Melanie Hoskin, had received multiple payment links for a limited edition release she had already paid for. A message promising a return by Wednesday evening had been deleted, leaving no timeframe.
